target_customer: Buy-side institutions (hedge funds, asset managers) trading US Treasuries
problem: US Treasury trading was dominated by dealers and dealer-run venues; Direct Match aimed to offer an anonymous all-to-all central limit order book.
business_model: Trading venue fees on matched Treasury trades

founders.name: Galen Simmons
founders.background_notes: YC lists him under former founders. Marketsmedia names Jim Greco as CEO in 2016; a search summary said Jim Greco and Kristi Neller launched the firm, not verified.

exit.reason: Its clearing partner withdrew weeks before the planned March 2016 launch, citing a conflict of interest; press named State Street. The CEO said the original business would not proceed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A regulated trading venue needing matching engine, connectivity and a clearing arrangement.

defensibility.rationale: A liquidity network would be hard to copy once running, but it never launched and depended on a clearing partner.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents later planned new venues around the time of Direct Match's exit per trade press; the direct cause of closure was clearing.

market_need_then: The Treasury market was dealer centric in 2014 and the company claimed commitments from about 60 clients before launch per Markets Media.

branding.domain_note: Used directmatchx.com; the host did not resolve from this session.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name with no brand press found.

pivots.to: Merger with OpenBondX to share a clearing link via Wedbush
pivots.why: Revival after clearing partner loss, per Bloomberg headline summary

outcome_analysis: Direct Match raised about $9 million and reported commitments from roughly 60 clients, but the business ended in August 2016 after its clearing partner withdrew weeks before the March 2016 launch, so it never completed a trade. Trade press blamed bank control of Treasury market plumbing. It was later reported to merge with OpenBondX in December 2016. The clearing failure is the sourced cause; the other factor reflects that the original model stopped.
notes: The $9M total is reported by Markets Media (single outlet, investors not named, no date); amount treated as total raised and labelled other. Business Insider and Bloomberg were only seen as search results. A later merger with OpenBondX was reported, so the YC Inactive status and shutdown reflect the original business. Competitor entries were left out because the sources describing BrokerTec and eSpeed as incumbents are undated. directmatchx.com did not resolve. I chose could_not_raise_next_round loosely; sources do not state fundraising failure, so treat that factor as low confidence.
